_comment: Dasher v6 cross-platform capability matrix — THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Rendered at https://dasher.at/status/. How to update: https://dasher.at/developers/feature-parity/. Validated by scripts/validate-feature-status.mjs in CI.

meta.v5_baseline: Dasher v5 shipped native frontends for Windows, Linux/GTK, macOS and iOS (Android had a separate community project (acl33/AndroidDasher); Mac/iPhone were unmaintained by the 5.0 beta). Input covered mouse, stylus/tablet, touch, multitouch, tilt, joystick (Linux) and socket input (the conduit for eye/gaze trackers). Notable v5 features: game/training mode, eye-tracker autocalibration, PPM family language models, Kanji/Pinyin conversion, and three TTS backends (SAPI / speech-dispatcher / flite).

status_legend.beta: Available but in beta / behind a flag
status_legend.not-supported: Not available — usually a platform limitation

features.title: Pointer / eye-gaze input
features.notes: Core pointer model. Eye-gaze trackers drive the cursor via socket input. visionOS uses native eye gaze + pinch.

features.title: Direct touch input
features.notes: Multi-touch on touchscreens and trackpads.

features.title: Single / dual switch scanning
features.notes: Apple exposes a dedicated switchesOnly access method with switch profiles (4 slots, key capture, scan rate). GTK supports keyboard-key assignment via remapping.

features.title: Joystick / gamepad input
features.notes: GTK uses SDL3 for full gamepad support (axes, buttons, haptic/rumble). Apple declares joystick in its access-method enum but the backing service is not yet implemented.

features.title: Tilt to steer (device tilt)
features.notes: iOS uses CoreMotion accelerometer with deadzone calibration. v5 had this on iPhone.

features.title: Socket / external cursor input
features.notes: Primary conduit for eye trackers and external assistive apps. In v5 this used a UDP coordinate protocol.

features.title: Hand tracking
features.notes: visionOS drives the pointer natively from pinch + hand position. Other platforms do not expose a hand-tracking pointer source.

macos.reason: Hand tracking APIs did not exist

ios.reason: Hand tracking APIs did not exist

features.title: Continuous (always moving)
features.notes: Dasher zooms continuously towards the cursor position. The default Dasher experience on every platform.

features.title: Dwell to select
features.notes: Cursor pauses in a zone for a dwell time to select. visionOS has a dwell indicator.

features.title: Click / tap to zoom
features.notes: Each click advances the zoom one step. Apple exposes pressToMove and clickToZoom selection methods.

features.title: Direct mode (tap boxes)
features.notes: Screen is divided into letter boxes that you tap directly. macOS implements this via Accessibility API text injection (directBoxes selection method).

ios.reason: No Accessibility API for text injection

features.title: Haptic / rumble feedback
features.notes: GTK uses SDL3 haptic/rumble for gamepad feedback.

features.title: Dasher canvas rendering
features.notes: Frontend renders the draw-command buffer produced by DasherCore. v5 used native canvas/OpenGL per platform.

features.title: Colour palette selection
features.notes: DasherCore ships 22 colour palettes. Apple exposes a palette picker; GTK exposes SyncedColorDropdown with live swatches.

features.title: Custom font family & size
features.notes: Apple offers 10 font families + size slider. GTK uses FontDialogButton (family/style/weight/size).

features.title: Left / right-handed layout
features.notes: Dasher can render left-to-right or right-to-left to suit handedness. Provided by DasherCore.

gtk.reason: Canvas follows OS; window chrome does not yet

features.title: PPM prediction (default model)
features.notes: Prediction by Partial Matching — the default language model. Provided by DasherCore to every frontend.

features.title: Alternative models (Word / Mixture / CTW)
features.dasher_core_dep: LMRegistry (Word id 1, Mixture id 2, CTW id 3)
features.notes: DasherCore registers 4 pluggable language models. Word caches context, Mixture combines PPM + Word, CTW is Context Tree Weighting.

features.title: Adaptive learning (LM adapts as you type)
features.notes: Language model learns from entered text to improve predictions. GTK exposes an explicit toggle.

features.title: Alphabet & language selection
features.notes: v5 carried ~140 alphabet definitions; v6 expands to 622 via WorldAlphabets (9 curated + 486 autoConverted + 127 legacy).

features.title: Pinyin / CJK conversion
features.notes: DasherCore ships Japanese alphabet files and a dedicated conversion system.

features.title: Spoken output (text-to-speech)
features.notes: Apple: swift-tts-wrapper (21 engine backends, voice/rate/pitch/volume). Windows: DotNetTtsWrapper. GTK: rust-tts-wrapper (placeholder, behind HAS_TTS flag). v5: SAPI (Windows), speech-dispatcher (Linux), flite (iOS).

features.title: Speak typed text on stop
features.dasher_core_dep: Output text stream + GameModule stop event
features.notes: Reads accumulated text aloud when the user stops Dasher. Part of the Apple Speech settings tab.

features.title: Copy text to clipboard
features.notes: Apple offers Copy and Copy All. GTK offers Copy and Copy All.

features.title: Paste / insert text
features.notes: Paste clipboard contents into Dasher's text buffer. GTK has Paste button; Apple has Paste (iOS).

features.title: System-wide direct text entry
features.notes: Injects text directly into other applications. macOS uses the Accessibility API (Direct Mode). Similar to an OS keyboard.

ios.reason: No Accessibility API for text injection

features.title: Save output to file
features.notes: macOS supports Save/Open file. GTK supports PDF screenshot export (F8).

features.title: Undo / redo typed text
features.notes: GTK has Undo/Redo buttons. v5 did not have undo.

features.title: PDF / screenshot export
features.notes: GTK supports PDF screenshot export (F8 key).

features.title: Control mode (text editing via Dasher nodes)
features.notes: Special control nodes appear in the zooming interface for text editing actions: select all, copy, move cursor, delete, etc. Lets you edit without leaving Dasher. Was a v5 feature; Windows is the first v6 frontend to wire it.

features.title: Grouped settings UI (by usage context)
features.notes: Apple: 6 tabs (Customization/Input/Language/Output/Speech/Game Mode). GTK: PreferencesWindow with StackSidebar + dynamic per-module grids. See dasher-design-guide for the normative structure.

features.title: Auto-discover engine parameters
features.notes: GTK auto-discovers all DasherCore parameters at runtime and builds settings UI dynamically with Synced* widgets (7 widget types).

features.title: Save / load user settings
features.notes: DasherCore persists settings as XML. All frontends load/save via the engine.

features.title: User-facing speed control
features.notes: GTK exposes a dedicated speed slider; Apple has speed in Customization tab. DasherCore also has auto-speed control.

features.title: Button / key remapping
features.notes: GTK supports live key recording for button assignment. Apple supports switch key capture (4 profiles).

features.title: Multiple UI languages
features.notes: Apple ships 9 UI locale translations. DasherCore carries 33 locale string files.

macos.reason: Engine strings localised; UI chrome still English

ios.reason: Engine strings localised; UI chrome still English

visionos.reason: Engine strings localised; UI chrome still English

windows.reason: Engine strings localised; UI chrome still English

features.title: Gamified training (Game Mode)
features.notes: DasherCore's GameModule tracks target text, correct/wrong/remaining characters, and a help path. Apple has Game Mode fully wired with custom text file support. GTK has the button but it is not wired.

features.title: Custom game / training text files
features.notes: Apple lets you load custom text files as Game Mode targets.

features.title: System-wide iOS keyboard extension
features.notes: Apple ships a keyboard extension on iOS that shares settings with the main app via a shared app group. Low-memory tuning for the extension process.

ios.reason: Standalone app only, no extension API

features.title: visionOS app
features.notes: Apple ships a visionOS app using eye gaze + pinch + dwell indicator.

features.title: Shared settings (app & keyboard extension)
features.notes: Apple uses a shared app group so the iOS keyboard extension and the main app share the same settings and user dictionary.

features.title: Privacy-preserving analytics & crash reporting
features.notes: Opt-in analytics via self-hosted PostHog (see RFC 0001). No text content ever collected. Windows ships posthog-dotnet SDK. Apple ships posthog-ios. GTK planned.

visionos.reason: SDK linked; opt-in prompt not yet shown

features.title: Lucide icon set
features.notes: Unified cross-platform icon library (see RFC 0002). Apple uses lucide-icons-swift, Windows uses Lucide.Avalonia, GTK will use the Lucide TTF font.

features.title: v5 to v6 settings migration
features.notes: One-shot migration: detects v5 data, translates registry/XML preferences to v6 equivalents, copies custom alphabets/colours/control/training files. See RFC 0005. Shipped on Windows and macOS.

ios.reason: No v5 iOS app to migrate from

visionos.reason: No v5 visionOS app to migrate from

android.reason: No v5 Android app in this lineage

features.title: Typing rate display (WPM / CPS)
features.notes: Live typing speed over a rolling window, computed engine-side (RFC 0012). Apple shows WPM, max, and average; web shows WPM and accuracy from its own engine.

features.title: Node-tree (custom) rendering
features.notes: A second rendering path that exposes the live node tree so a frontend can draw 3D / VR / custom views (RFC 0013). The engine API is implemented and tested; no production frontend uses it. The DasherMac cube branch is experimental and buggy. Future hope: a spatial eye-tracked port (e.g. Meta Quest). Not planned for every platform.

macos.reason: Engine ready; experimental cube branch (buggy, unmerged)

features.title: Image labels for alphabet symbols
features.notes: Optional image= attribute on alphabet symbols (RFC 0014). Engine + macOS frontend ready, but dynamic image sizing is hard and no bundled alphabet uses images yet. The phoneme-symbol use case is experimental. Not planned for every platform.

macos.reason: Engine + frontend ready; no alphabet ships images yet

ios.reason: Frontend does not consume the API

visionos.reason: Frontend does not consume the API
